standard_prerequisites.name: On a scheme with the resolution property every perfect complex is represented by a bounded complex of finite locally free modules, and the representation is unique up to the usual homotopy arguments
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 10235-10237 and used throughout
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the representatives on which the alternating sum map is defined and the maps needed for well definedness.

standard_prerequisites.name: A surjection of finite locally free modules is locally split, so its kernel is again finite locally free
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the additivity of the alternating sum on short exact sequences of complexes.

standard_prerequisites.name: An acyclic bounded complex can be filtered by short exact sequences whose terms are the images of the differentials
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the alternating sum vanishes on acyclic complexes, which is the second ingredient of well definedness.

standard_prerequisites.name: Stupid truncations sit in distinguished triangles whose third term is a single module placed in one degree
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows by induction that the class of a complex in K-theory is the alternating sum of its terms, giving surjectivity.

core_obligations: Construct a map from the K-theory of perfect complexes to the K-theory of vector bundles by sending the class of a bounded complex of finite locally free modules to the alternating sum of the classes of its terms (proof lines 10235-10250).

Show additivity on a surjection of such complexes: the kernels of the termwise surjections are finite locally free because the surjections are locally split, so the alternating sums add (proof lines 10251-10258).
Show that the alternating sum of an acyclic complex vanishes, by breaking the complex into short exact sequences along its differentials and arguing by descending induction (proof lines 10259-10284).

Conclude well definedness: two complexes representing the same object are connected by quasi-isomorphisms from a third one, the cone of a quasi-isomorphism is acyclic, and the vanishing just proved forces the alternating sums to agree (proof lines 10285-10330).

Note additivity on distinguished triangles follows from the same cone argument, obtaining a homomorphism of abelian groups, and check that the composite with the comparison map is the identity (proof lines 10331-10338).

Using the distinguished triangles of stupid truncations and induction, show that the class of a complex is the alternating sum of its shifted terms, which gives surjectivity and finishes the proof (proof lines 10339-10353).
proof_roadmap: Define the alternating sum map and reduce well definedness to two computations (proof lines 10235-10250).
Additivity on surjections and vanishing on acyclic complexes (proof lines 10251-10284).
Well definedness via cones of quasi-isomorphisms (proof lines 10285-10330).
Identity of the composite and surjectivity via truncations (proof lines 10331-10353).
